Corning is a materials science company in Corning, New York, founded 1851, making specialty glass (Gorilla Glass for smartphones), optical fiber and cable, ceramics and life science labware, supplying Apple, Samsung, telecom carriers and data center customers. Revenue is around $13-14 billion. Listed on the NYSE (GLW). Known for Gorilla Glass and Pyrex heritage, B2B largely, with decent technology brand awareness.

James Hardie Industries is an Irish-domiciled fibre cement maker, with North American operations in Chicago, selling HardiePlank siding, trim, backer board and decking to homebuilders, contractors and homeowners in the US, Australia, New Zealand and Europe. It acquired Azek in 2025 for about 8.75 billion dollars. It is listed on the NYSE (JHX) and ASX. It is a well known building products brand in the US among builders and renovators, and its marketing is aimed at homeowners.

Omega Healthcare Investors is a healthcare real estate investment trust, headquartered in Hunt Valley (Cockeysville), Maryland, that owns skilled nursing facilities, senior housing and related properties leased to operators across the US and the UK. It earns lease and mortgage income and is listed on the NYSE (OHI). It owns roughly 900 properties with operators including Ensign and Genesis-related entities. It is a B2B REIT with little consumer brand awareness.

TopBuild is a Daytona Beach, Florida installer and distributor of insulation and building products, serving residential and commercial builders through TruTeam installation and Specialty Distribution businesses, which it expanded by acquiring Specialty Products & Insulation and Progressive Roofing. It is listed on the NYSE (BLD), with revenue of about 5 billion dollars. Customers are builders and contractors. It is a B2B brand, which has done limited sports sponsorship, with little consumer awareness.

United Site Services is the largest US provider of portable toilets, temporary fencing, restroom trailers and site services, based in Meridian, Idaho (it also operated from Atlanta), serving construction sites, events, and municipalities with branches nationwide. It is private equity owned by Platinum Equity, which acquired it in 2017 and formed it by merging regional providers. It operates a large fleet of units and trucks. It is a B2B service brand visible at events and construction sites.

Quintain Estates & Development is a UK property developer and investor best known for Wembley Park in north London, where it has built thousands of build-to-rent homes (Tipi, Wembley Park brand), student housing, offices and retail near Wembley Stadium. It was acquired by Lone Star Funds in 2015 and is based in London. Revenue is rents and sales. Wembley Park is a recognised London destination brand.

about: Sika is a Swiss specialty chemicals company founded in 1910 in Baar, Zug, that makes construction chemicals and industrial products: sealants, adhesives, waterproofing, concrete admixtures, roofing and automotive bonding materials. Customers are builders, contractors and car and industrial manufacturers in more than 100 countries, with sales above CHF 11 billion and around 34,000 employees. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (SIKA). Strong B2B brand, with consumer exposure through DIY stores and motorsport partnerships.

American Bath Group is an Irving, Texas manufacturer of bathroom products, including bathtubs, showers and related fixtures under brands such as Aquatic and Lasco Bathware, selling to home improvement chains, builders and distributors in North America. It is privately held, and Crunchbase shows funding of about $2.3 billion. B2B supplier, mostly sold through retail partners, with low consumer brand awareness. Details of ownership were not confirmed.

about: Builders FirstSource is the largest US supplier of building materials, manufactured components and construction services to professional homebuilders, remodelers and contractors, selling lumber, trusses, windows, doors, millwork and installation, from more than 500 locations across the US. Headquartered in Irving, Texas, and listed on the NYSE under BLDR, with annual revenue around $15 billion. Formed from the 2015 merger with ProBuild. B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Gibraltar Industries is a Buffalo, New York manufacturer of building products, including residential mail and storage products, ventilation, renewable energy racking and structures for solar, and agtech greenhouse and infrastructure. Customers are home improvement retailers, builders, utilities and solar developers, and it is listed on Nasdaq under ROCK. Revenue is around $1.1 billion. B2B and retail-channel supplier with modest consumer brand awareness.

Weyerhaeuser is a Seattle-based timber real estate investment trust and one of the world's largest private owners of timberlands, with over 10 million acres in the US, plus wood products manufacturing producing lumber, oriented strand board and engineered wood. Customers are homebuilders and building-supply dealers. Founded in 1900 and listed on the NYSE under WY. Revenue is around $7 billion. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness beyond its name.

Arada is a Sharjah-based property developer headquartered in Dubai, known for master-planned communities such as Aljada and Masaar, with project values in the tens of billions of dirhams. Customers are homebuyers and investors in the UAE and international markets. It is privately owned by Sharjah-linked investors. A visible regional real estate brand in the UAE. Revenue comes from property sales and rental, and the company has delivered thousands of homes. It is a well-known real estate brand in the UAE, with marketing aimed at homebuyers.

Granite Construction is a Watsonville, California civil construction and materials company that builds roads, highways, dams, bridges and other infrastructure, mainly in the western United States, and produces aggregates and asphalt. Revenue is about 4 billion dollars. Customers are public agencies. Listed on NYSE (GVA), it was founded in 1922. B2B infrastructure builder with little public brand awareness. Revenue comes from construction contracts and materials sales, and the company has about 5 billion dollars in revenue. It is a B2B brand with moderate public profile, listed on NYSE (GVA).

Griffon Corporation is a New York-based diversified holding company that owns consumer and professional products: Ames tools and garden products, Hunter Fan, AMES, True Temper and Clopay garage doors. Customers are homeowners and retailers such as Home Depot and Lowe's. Listed on NYSE (GFF). Its brands are known in North American homes, but the group is not a consumer name.

UltraTech Cement is a Mumbai-based Aditya Birla Group company, the largest cement maker in India and third-largest globally outside China, with capacity of about 150 million tonnes a year, producing grey and white cement and ready-mix concrete. Listed on the Bombay and National Stock Exchanges (ULTRACEMCO). Mostly sold through dealers to builders and households, with a consumer brand recognised in India.

Denver-based construction materials company producing aggregates, cement and ready-mix concrete across the US and British Columbia. Founded in 2009 and listed on the NYSE (SUM), it bought Argos USA's cement business in 2024. Agreed in 2025 to be acquired by Quikrete Holdings. Customers are contractors and public infrastructure agencies. B2B brand.

Elkhart, Indiana-based supplier of components for the RV, marine, and manufactured housing industries, listed on Nasdaq (PATK). Founded in 1959, it makes and distributes cabinets, doors, flooring, countertops and electronics, and serves powersports firms. Customers are manufacturers and RV makers such as Thor and Forest River. Revenue about 3.7 billion dollars. B2B brand.

Swedish engineering group in Stockholm, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (SAND), producing mining equipment, rock tools and metal-cutting tools (Sandvik Coromant). Founded in 1862, it has divisions for mining and rock solutions, rock processing and manufacturing and machining solutions, and spun off its materials business as Alleima in 2022. About 40,000 employees. Revenue about SEK 120 billion. Strong B2B brand.

Brandywine Realty Trust is a Philadelphia-based real estate investment trust (NYSE: BDN) that owns, develops and manages office and mixed-use properties, with its main presence in Philadelphia, Austin and the Washington DC area. Revenue comes from rent from corporate tenants. Founded as a REIT in the 1990s, it holds a portfolio of several million square feet. Mainly B2B; little consumer awareness beyond its local markets.

Doman Building Materials Group is a Vancouver-based wholesale distributor of building materials, including lumber, treated wood, plywood and specialty products, serving home improvement retailers and contractors across Canada and the US. It merged with CanWel Building Materials Group (TSX: CWX) in 2019 to form a larger Canadian distributor. B2B distribution with no consumer profile.

about: Eco Material Technologies is a Utah-based producer and distributor of fly ash and other supplementary cementitious materials used to make lower-carbon concrete, sourcing from coal power plants and sold to concrete and cement producers across North America. It is private-equity backed (Charlesbank is among its investors). Customers are construction and building-materials companies. B2B niche with very low public awareness.

about: Grasim Industries is a flagship of India's Aditya Birla Group, headquartered in Mumbai and listed on the NSE/BSE. It is among the world's largest viscose staple fibre producers and a major chlor-alkali, cement-via-UltraTech, and chemicals producer, and has expanded into paints (Birla Opus) and building materials. Operates widely across India with revenue above INR 1 trillion. Group brand highly visible in India, though Grasim itself is industrial and B2B.

Infra.Market is an Indian B2B e-commerce and construction materials platform, based in Thane, Maharashtra, that supplies cement, steel, tiles, plumbing and other building products to contractors and developers, and manufactures its own products such as ready-mix concrete and tiles. Founded in 2016, it became a unicorn, backed by Tiger Global and Nexus; revenue is in the billions of dollars equivalent. B2B brand known in the Indian construction sector, little consumer profile.

Nykredit Realkredit is a Copenhagen-based Danish mortgage credit institution, the country's largest mortgage lender, owned by Foreningen Nykredit and the Nykredit group. It also owns Totalkredit and operates retail banking with Nykredit Bank. Customers are homeowners, farmers and businesses. Highly recognised in Denmark and a sponsor of Danish sport.

Beazer Homes is an Atlanta-based homebuilder that designs and builds single-family houses and townhomes in about 13 US states, including Arizona, Texas, Florida, the Carolinas, Georgia and Tennessee. It focuses on first-time and move-up buyers, with its Energy Smart Homes branding, and delivers about 4,000 homes a year, with revenue of roughly 2.5 billion dollars. It also provides mortgage and title services. It is listed on the NYSE (BZH). Regional consumer brand with moderate local visibility.

Flock Safety is an Atlanta-based public safety technology company founded in 2017. It makes solar-powered automatic licence plate reader cameras, gunshot detection, video and drone first-responder systems, sold by subscription to law enforcement agencies, neighbourhood associations, businesses and campuses, and used in thousands of US cities. It has raised over 1 billion dollars, with a valuation of about 7.5 billion dollars. Privately held. B2B and government brand, controversial for privacy and surveillance issues.

Piramal Capital & Housing Finance is the housing finance and lending arm of India's Piramal Enterprises, based in Mumbai, offering home loans, loans against property, construction finance and mid-market lending to builders and retail borrowers. It is a subsidiary of Piramal Enterprises and earns interest income. It has raised about 1 billion dollars from bonds and bank funding, and came from the 2021 merger of Dewan Housing Finance's assets into the Piramal group. Financial brand with moderate awareness in India.

ADENTRA Group, formerly Hardwoods Distribution, is a Langley, British Columbia distributor of architectural building products, mainly cabinet components, panels, doors, decorative hardware, edgebanding and flooring. It serves cabinet makers, builders and dealers across North America and the UK, with revenue of around 3 billion Canadian dollars. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ADEN). B2B distributor with no consumer awareness, so sponsorship fit would be limited to corporate hospitality.

China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC) is one of the world's largest construction groups, based in Beijing, a state-owned enterprise building railways, highways, metros, bridges, tunnels, airports and housing, plus real estate and equipment manufacturing, in China and overseas, including Africa, Asia and the Middle East. Revenue is above 1 trillion yuan. Listed on the Shanghai and Hong Kong exchanges (601186, 1186). B2B contractor with a big corporate profile and no real consumer brand.

Internacional de Ceramica (Interceramic) is a Mexican building materials firm based in Chihuahua, producing and selling ceramic and porcelain floor and wall tile, plus natural stone, plumbing and related products through its own Interceramic stores in Mexico, the US and Latin America. Customers are homeowners, builders and distributors. It is listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange. Well-known flooring brand in Mexico, with a retail chain and consumer advertising.

US green steel technology company, spun out of MIT, developing molten oxide electrolysis to make steel without carbon emissions and to produce metals such as tantalum and vanadium. Based in Woburn, Massachusetts, with pilot work in Massachusetts and Brazil. Customers are steelmakers and mining companies licensing the process. Backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, ArcelorMittal and other investors, with total funding of about $530 million. Deep-tech B2B brand, known in cleantech and heavy industry circles only.

US real estate investment trust based in Westlake Village, California, that invests in senior housing and skilled nursing properties, leasing them to healthcare operators on long-term triple-net leases. Listed on the NYSE (LTC) and operating since 1992. Income comes from rent and interest on mortgage loans. Funding of about $397 million shown for October 2026. Financial investor with no consumer brand profile.

BuildDirect is a Canadian online marketplace for flooring and building materials, based in Vancouver, founded in 2002, selling hardwood, vinyl, tile and decking to homeowners and contractors in the US and Canada, mostly through its website. It raised about $202 million. Customers are renovators and contractors. Moderate consumer brand awareness for online building supplies.

Post Brothers is a Philadelphia real estate developer and housing operator, building and managing luxury residential apartment properties and mixed-use projects, with a focus on urban sites in cities such as Philadelphia and Dallas. It earns rents and development gains. Crunchbase shows about $170 million in funding, with the latest round in October 2025, likely equity or capital for projects. Privately held. Locally known in its property markets, but not a national consumer brand.

about: Ke Holdings (Beike) operates Ke.com, China's largest online and offline housing transaction and services platform, connecting real estate agents, brokerages (including Lianjia), developers and consumers for home sales, rentals, renovations and home services. It earns commissions and service fees. Based in Beijing, it is listed on the NYSE (BEKE) and in Hong Kong (2423). Hundreds of thousands of agents and a strong consumer presence in China's housing market, with no sponsorship tradition outside China.

Beacon Building Products (Beacon Roofing Supply) is a Herndon, Virginia distributor of roofing materials, plus complementary products such as siding, waterproofing and insulation, with over 500 branches across the US and Canada, selling to roofing contractors and builders. Listed on Nasdaq (BECN) until QXO, the building products distribution company led by Brad Jacobs, acquired it in 2025 for about $11 billion. B2B distributor, known to contractors and with no consumer awareness.

MITER Brands is a US manufacturer of residential windows and doors, formed by combining MI Windows and Doors and Milgard, with brands including Milgard, MI Windows and Doors, and Fibertec. It sells through dealers, distributors and home centres to builders and homeowners. Crunchbase shows a Fife, Washington location, which matches Milgard's base, and about $700 million in funding, with the latest round in March 2024. Privately held. Known in the building trades, with moderate homeowner recognition.

about: Parsons Corporation is a Chantilly, Virginia engineering, technology and construction company, listed on the NYSE (PSN), providing services for defence, intelligence, cyber, space and critical infrastructure, such as transport projects, to government and commercial customers. It employs around 18,000 people and was founded in 1944. Revenue is from government and project contracts. B2B and government brand, well known in defence and infrastructure circles, with no consumer awareness.

The AZEK Company is a Chicago-based maker of outdoor living products, mainly TimberTech composite and PVC decking, railing, AZEK Exteriors trim and mouldings, and StruXure pergolas, sold through dealers and distributors to homeowners, builders and contractors. It was listed on the NYSE (AZEK) and acquired by James Hardie in 2025 for about $8.75 billion. Revenue was about $1.4 billion a year. Recognised in residential building products and by homeowners planning decks.

The ODP Corporation is a Boca Raton, Florida business-to-business and consumer distributor of office products and supplies, owning Office Depot and OfficeMax retail stores, ODP Business Solutions and the supply chain unit Veyer. It serves businesses, schools, governments and consumers. It was listed on Nasdaq (ODP) and was acquired by Atlas Holdings in 2025 in a take-private deal valued at about $1 billion. Strong consumer brand awareness in the US, with a large retail footprint.

Wienerberger is a Vienna-based international building materials group, listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange (WIE), and one of the world's largest brick makers. It produces clay blocks (Porotherm), facing bricks (Terca), roof tiles (Koramic), concrete pavers (Semmelrock) and plastic and ceramic pipes (Pipelife), with plants in about 30 countries. Customers are builders, contractors and distributors. Founded in 1819. B2B brand with some consumer recognition in European home building.

Ming Shing Group is a Hong Kong construction group, based in Kowloon City, offering civil engineering, foundation and site formation work and related building services, mainly as a contractor on public and private projects in Hong Kong. The Crunchbase entry records roughly $483M of funding, most recently in August 2025, and describes it as an engineering and construction firm. Limited public information is available beyond that, and it is a B2B contractor with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Heckler & Koch is a German small-arms manufacturer producing pistols, assault rifles (HK416, G36), submachine guns (MP5) and machine guns. Customers are armed forces, police and security agencies in NATO and allied countries, plus some civilian sport shooters, and it earns money from weapons, accessories and service contracts. Based in Oberndorf am Neckar, near Rottweil, it employs around 1,000 people and has revenue near 400-500 million euros. Strong defence-industry brand but a controversial one, which makes consumer sponsorship difficult.

Oldcastle BuildingEnvelope is a Dallas-based North American manufacturer of architectural glass, aluminium framing, curtain walls and storefront systems for commercial buildings. Customers are architects, glaziers, contractors and developers, with revenue from product sales and installation. It is part of CRH, the Irish-headquartered building materials group, which is listed on the NYSE and London. Crunchbase shows about 300 million dollars of funding. B2B building products brand with little consumer awareness.

about: Terra CO2 Technologies is a Golden, Colorado cleantech company producing supplementary cementitious materials from glass, designed to replace part of the cement in concrete and cut carbon emissions. Customers are concrete producers, builders and infrastructure owners. The company is venture-backed and sells the material to concrete makers by volume, aiming to cut the large carbon footprint of cement production. Crunchbase shows about 281 million dollars of funding. Early-stage B2B materials company with little public awareness.

about: Argos USA is the United States arm of Colombian cement group Grupo Argos, headquartered in Atlanta with operations in the southeast, and supplies cement, ready-mix concrete and aggregates to builders, contractors and infrastructure projects. The business was later combined with Summit Materials in a transaction announced in 2024. Crunchbase shows about 1.05 billion dollars raised. A B2B building materials producer with little consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Argos USA operates as a construction material company.

about: Ambuja Cement is one of India's largest cement producers, headquartered in Mumbai, with plants and grinding units across the country and annual capacity of roughly 70 million tonnes, selling cement to builders, contractors and homebuyers under the Ambuja, ACC and other brands. Adani Group took control in 2022 when it bought Holcim's Indian businesses, and Ambuja is listed on the NSE and BSE as AMBUJACEM. A visible building-materials brand across India, with mainly B2B and retail dealer reach.

Cornerstone Building Brands is a Cary, North Carolina manufacturer of exterior building products for residential and commercial construction, including vinyl siding, windows, fencing and railing, metal buildings and coatings, under brands such as Ply Gem, Atrium and NCI. It sells through distributors, home centres and builders across North America and has revenue of several billion dollars. Clayton, Dubilier & Rice took the company private in 2022. Customers are builders and contractors, with modest awareness among homeowners.
